eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Frame Transactions was the central proposal discussed, covering its CFI status, spec updates, guarantor change, L2 adoption, and open questions.

moments.context: Marc introduced the call by noting EIP-8141 was recently proposed as a headliner for Hegota, was CFI'd, but ultimately not selected by client teams due to concerns about mempool, statelessness, privacy, and post-quantum.
Ivo from Ambire said frame transactions solve the problem of existing EOAs not being able to use AA features and address the clunkiness of 4337.
Agus from Polygon said they strongly support frame transactions as-is because they allow full flexibility; a more constrained solution would likely not be adopted by their team.
Lightclient described the design philosophy behind 8141, emphasizing post-quantum support, reducing reliance on centralized relayers, and supporting FOCIL compatibility.
Chris aggregated feedback he had gathered on why some teams do not want 8141, citing overhead and complexity carried for future features they may not use.
Derek provided an update on the guarantor concept where a payer frame can precede sender validation, allowing the mempool to skip expensive sender validation if the payer is valid.
Ben Adams noted he tightened up the 8141 spec and it was merged, but also introduced complementary unbundled EIPs as an alternative layering approach.
David from Trust Wallet argued 8141 should be merged to prevent wallets from building proprietary automation solutions, and noted adoption timelines require preparation time.
Derek outlined the three core adoption barriers 8141 addresses: smart contract auditing burden, relayer dependence, and cross-chain reliability.
Prestwich questioned whether 8141 should proceed given that several promised benefits like ERC20 sponsorship and post-quantum support are still in ideation or require follow-on EIPs.

eips.title: Set Code for EOAs
eips.summary: Referenced repeatedly as the current AA mechanism that frame transactions build upon, with discussion of its adoption trajectory and hardware wallet limitations.

moments.context: Ivo noted that 7702 partially solved EOA upgrade paths but hardware wallets still don't fully support it, limiting practical AA adoption.
David from Trust Wallet pushed back on claims of low 7702 adoption, citing nearly 100 million weekly 7702 transactions and meaningful TrustWallet traffic.

eips.summary: Referenced as the existing AA standard that native AA proposals aim to improve upon or replace, described as clunky and bloated.

moments.context: Ivo described 4337 as clunky and bloated, positioning frame transactions as a practical improvement over it.
Derek noted TrustWallet adopted 7702-4337, and discussed how native AA eliminates the relayer dependency that 4337 requires.

eips.title: Keystore Accounts
eips.summary: Keystore Accounts was described by Chris from Base as a more defined alternative to 8141 that addresses performance concerns with explicit call ordering.

moments.context: Chris summarized 8130 as trying to address performance issues while remaining general, with explicit ordering of operations to reduce DoS risks, though less flexible than 8141.

eips.summary: Agus asked in chat whether the guarantor concept in 8141 is somewhat similar to EIP-5189.

moments.context: Agus asked in chat whether the guarantor idea for frame transactions is similar to 5189.

eips.title: Contract Payer Transaction
eips.summary: Contract Payer Transaction was presented by Ben Adams as an unbundled alternative approach to gas sponsorship using a one-to-one signer-vault model.

moments.context: Ben Adams described 8223 as allowing a contract vault to accept a specific EOA signer, enabling lightweight mempool validation by checking ETH balance without invoking the EVM.
Ben highlighted the difference from 8141's sponsorship model: 8223 restricts sponsorship to the user's own assets in a different account rather than arbitrary third-party sponsors.

eips.title: Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode
eips.summary: Transaction assertions via state diff opcode was presented as complementary to frame transactions for preventing phishing and drainer attacks.

moments.context: Fredrik described EIP-7906 as enabling users to set revert conditions on transactions if outcomes exceed approved state changes, addressing phishing and drainer attacks.
Fredrik noted the next step is building a proof-of-concept demo, potentially with the Ethrex team, and creating tests for inclusion in a future hard fork.
Alex Forshtat, the author, confirmed 7906 works well with frame transactions but does not require them, and expressed interest in collaborating with Ethrex on a demo.

eips.title: Add BLAKE2 compression function `F` precompile
eips.summary: Prestwich cited his involvement with EIP-152 as a cautionary example against designing EIPs for not-yet-understood future use cases.

moments.context: Prestwich said in chat that designing EIPs to support future use cases that are not fully understood has typically been a mistake, citing his involvement with EIP-152.

eips.title: Fee market change for ETH 1.0 chain
eips.summary: Chris mentioned in chat that legacy and 1559 transaction type deprecation would be needed if using an EOA-based account with 8130.

moments.context: Chris noted in chat that 8130 handles key rotation including ECDSA deprecation, with the caveat that 1559/legacy tx deprecation would also be needed for EOA-based accounts.

eips.title: Code-Controlled EOA Delegation
eips.summary: Referenced in chat as a proposal for deactivating a delegated EOA's key, relevant to ECDSA sunset discussions.

moments.context: Nico posted links to EIP-7851 and EIP-8151 in chat as proposals addressing EOA key deactivation and ecRecover awareness, noted as independent from 8141.

eips.title: Account Code Restricted ecRecover
eips.summary: Referenced in chat alongside EIP-7851 as a proposal for private key deactivation-aware ecRecover.

moments.context: Nico linked EIP-8151 in chat as a companion to EIP-7851 for making ecRecover aware of deactivated private keys.

eips.title: SETDELEGATE instruction
eips.summary: Linked in chat by lightclient as one of several proposals addressing ECDSA key management for EOAs.

moments.context: Lightclient shared links to EIP-7819 and EIP-7851 in chat as existing proposals for handling ECDSA key revocation.
